summary: Master hydrolysis constant derivations, degrees of hydrolysis, and exact pH formulas for all four salt types.

summaryBox.title: Hydrolysis Types
summaryBox.takeaway: WA-SB: pH > 7. SA-WB: pH < 7. WA-WB: pH depends on pK_a - pK_b (independent of C!).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SALT HYDROLYSIS TYPES
                                      │
     ┌──────────────────┬─────────────┴─────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼                           ▼                  ▼
STRONG ACID +          WEAK ACID +                 STRONG ACID +       WEAK ACID +
STRONG BASE            STRONG BASE                 WEAK BASE           WEAK BASE
(e.g., NaCl)           (e.g., CH₃COONa)            (e.g., NH₄Cl)       (e.g., CH₃COONH₄)
├── NO Hydrolysis      ├── Anionic Hydrolysis      ├── Cationic Hydrolysis├── Both Hydrolyze
└── Neutral (pH=7)     └── Alkaline (pH > 7)       └── Acidic (pH < 7) └── pH depends on K_a/K_b
conceptBreakdown.content: Salt hydrolysis is the interaction of salt cations or anions with water to alter the $[\text{H}^+] / [\text{OH}^-]$ balance, yielding acidic, basic, or neutral solutions.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 Comprehensive Hydrolysis Derivation Matrix
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Comprehensive Hydrolysis Derivation Matrix
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Strong Acid + Strong Base (SA + SB)** (e.g., $\text{NaCl}$): No Hydrolysis, $h = 0$, $[\text{H}^+] = 10^{-7}\text{ M} \implies \mathbf{\text{pH} = \frac{1}{2} \text{p}K_w = 7.00}$ (Neutral).

2. **Weak Acid + Strong Base (WA + SB)** (e.g., $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$): Anionic Hydrolysis ($K_h = K_w/K_a$), $h = \sqrt{K_w / (K_a C)}$, $[\text{OH}^-] = \sqrt{(K_w C)/K_a} \implies \mathbf{\text{pH} = \frac{1}{2} [\text{p}K_w + \text{p}K_a + \log_{10} C]}$ (Basic, $>7$).

3. **Strong Acid + Weak Base (SA + WB)** (e.g., $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$): Cationic Hydrolysis ($K_h = K_w/K_b$), $h = \sqrt{K_w / (K_b C)}$, $[\text{H}^+] = \sqrt{(K_w C)/K_b} \implies \mathbf{\text{pH} = \frac{1}{2} [\text{p}K_w - \text{p}K_b - \log_{10} C]}$ (Acidic, $<7$).

4. **Weak Acid + Weak Base (WA + WB)** (e.g., $\text{CH}_3\text{COONH}_4$): Both Cation & Anion Hydrolyze ($K_h = K_w / (K_a K_b)$), $h = \sqrt{K_w / (K_a K_b)}$ (No $C$!), $[\text{H}^+] = \sqrt{(K_w K_a)/K_b} \implies \mathbf{\text{pH} = \frac{1}{2} [\text{p}K_w + \text{p}K_a - \text{p}K_b]}$ (Concentration Independent!).

quickRevision: CH₃COONa: Anionic hydrolysis, pH = 1/2 [pK_w + pK_a + log C] > 7.
NH₄Cl: Cationic hydrolysis, pH = 1/2 [pK_w - pK_b - log C] < 7.
CH₃COONH₄: pH = 1/2 [pK_w + pK_a - pK_b] (independent of C).
Hydrolysis degree h = √(K_h / C) for single-ion hydrolysis.
